Repo: /workspace/SuperGrok1.5, branch claude/h100-audit-maximal. H100 sm_90. You are the SOLE builder now — the prior concurrent-session edit-war is OVER (those sessions were closed), so build freely and commit your verified work. Current state: 21/33 cells L3-TC, ALL parity-verified (tail-gate 21/21).

TASK: convert **SuperGrok11 (race key `supergrok`) and SuperGrok15 (`supergrok15`) on DECODER and VIT** to real L3-TC wgmma cells (4 cells), landing 21 -> 25/33. For MAMBA, land SG11/SG15 DORMANT (gated OUT of _L3_WGMMA_CELLS), exactly like looksam×mamba — the shared mamba-forward A/A/A determinism race blocks it.

REUSE THE EXISTING SAM 2nd-pass: the in-kernel SAM second fwd+bwd ALREADY EXISTS (built for looksam — see commits bab8914/fb997a9 and the looksam P2.4 block in fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh / fused_vit_megakernel.cuh). looksam writes `sam_dir = g_sam - g`; SG11/SG15 instead write **sharpness = (g_sam - g)^2** (the 2nd pass already produces g_sam — change only the elementwise write into st.sharpness), THEN run a per-tensor **meta-net mu precompute stage** feeding apply_optimizer<SuperGrok11/15>: mu = rescale * SharpnessMetaNet(g, sharpness); SG11 has a per-tensor cosine gate, SG15 a host-scalar gate. That stage is specified in INTEGRATION-OPTSTAGES.md §4 (SG11) / §5 (SG15), CPU-fp64-validated 9/9; the helpers sg11_precompute_mu_and_gate_for_tensor<32> / sg15_precompute_mu_for_tensor<32> are in opt_stages_precompute.cuh. **SharpnessMetaNet hidden_dim = 32** (NOT 64 — a known prior bug).

REFS: /workspace/.sam_spec.md (SAM-2nd-pass + ABI: st.sharpness already added), csrc/algorithms/supergrok11.h + supergrok15.h, opt_components.cuh (FusedOptState st.sharpness/st.mu/st.gate; apply tails for SuperGrok11/15), csrc/bindings/dispatch.cpp (wgmma_tail_opt_id: looksam=4/SG11=8/SG15=9), grokking_optimizers/dispatch.py (_FUSED_L3_REAL / _L3_WGMMA_CELLS), the looksam cells as the template, .audit_notes.md (SG11/15 history).

RULES: NO functionality suppression. Parity is the gate (SG-family ~3e-5, fp32 storage). Single-source math (supergrok11.h/sg15.h canonical; editing them => update scripts/check_math_single_source.py manifest). Portable header-only; no CUDA graphs.

BUILD: `python setup.py build_ext --inplace` (FAST incremental, ~25-170s; do NOT use `pip install -e .`). sccache is live (SCCACHE_DIR=/dev/shm/sccache). Export `TORCH_EXTENSIONS_DIR=/dev/shm/torch_ext TMPDIR=/dev/shm/tmp` so builds stay off the 30GB root.

GATES (CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY=/nonexistent): (1) `python -m tests.hw.test_l3tc_tail_gate` — existing cells stay green AND SG11/SG15 decoder/vit PASS (parity vs eager+canonical, A/A/A deterministic); register the new cells in the gate if needed. (2) `python wiring_check.py --require-all` — SG11/SG15 decoder/vit flip to PASS L3-TC-megakernel(wgmma); count 21 -> 25.

HONESTY: SG11/SG15 are expected parity-correct but will likely NOT grok (meta-net memorize-then-collapse, per .audit_notes.md). Goal = L3-TC + parity-clean; grok is a separate documented result, NOT a gate. Never fake/suppress to force grok.

COMMIT each verified-green cell/batch LOCALLY (never push), RAW gate evidence in the message (match the existing `h100 ...` cell commits), ending with: Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

RETURN: per-cell raw gate output (tail-gate + wiring_check showing SG11/SG15 dec/vit PASS), new count (expect 25/33), diff summary, build wall-time, honest grok note, and any cell that resisted (land what passes, report the rest).

1	# INTEGRATION-OPTSTAGES.md — wiring the in-kernel optimizer precompute stages
2	
3	**Scope.** This spec tells the binding/cell/codegen layer how to drive the
4	per-step PRECOMPUTE stages in `csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_stages_precompute.cuh` so
5	that every optimizer TAIL (`csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_components.cuh::apply_optimizer
6	<OptId>`) can run fully inside one persistent megakernel. It is a wiring
7	contract, not code: it does not touch `opt_components.cuh`,
8	`megakernel_codegen.py`, `dispatch.cpp`, `bindings.cpp`, or any
9	`supergrok2*`/`neuralgrok.py`/`grokadamw.py`/model-stage file (sibling-owned).
10	
11	Today only AdamW / Lion have a complete in-kernel tail (no precompute). The 9
12	non-trivial optimizers are classified below; the 4 STAGED ones get an upstream
13	stage that fills the `FusedOptState` fields their apply reads.
14	
15	---
16	
17	## 0. Verdict table (per-optimizer)
18	
19	| optimizer    | verdict        | what the apply reads | who produces it |
20	|--------------|----------------|----------------------|-----------------|
21	| grokfast     | NOTHING-NEEDED | (EMA fused in apply) | — `grokfast.h:63-65` |
22	| grokadamw    | NOTHING-NEEDED | (EMA fused in apply) | — `grokadamw.h:48-49` |
23	| neuralgrok   | NOTHING-NEEDED | (psi MLP inline)     | — `opt_components.cuh:222-229` → `neuralgrok.h:31-46` |
24	| looksam      | MODEL-COUPLED  | `st.sam_dir`         | **model stage** (2nd backward), `looksam.h:52-59` |
25	| prodigy      | STAGED         | `st.d_factor`        | `prodigy_precompute_*` |
26	| muon         | STAGED         | `st.orth`, `st.neg_lr_scale`, `st.decay_factor` | `muon_*` stage chain |
27	| supergrok11  | STAGED         | `st.mu`, `st.gate`   | `sg11_precompute_mu_and_gate_for_tensor` (per-tensor) |
28	| supergrok15  | STAGED         | `st.mu` (`st.gate` = host scalar) | `sg15_precompute_mu_for_tensor` (per-tensor) |
29	| supergrok2   | SKIP           | (sibling-owned)      | — |
30	
31	For the 3 NOTHING-NEEDED optimizers the codegen maps OptId → "no precompute
32	stage": their apply already runs a complete tail. `optimizer_needs_precompute
33	<Opt>::value` is `false` for them and a `static_assert` in
34	`optimizer_precompute_stage<Opt>` rejects an accidental instantiation.
35	
36	---
37	
38	## 1. The `PrecomputeWorkspace` POD (host allocation)
39	
40	The cross-CTA stages reduce through global scratch grouped in
41	`PrecomputeWorkspace` (mirrors `PersistentContext`: one POD so the codegen kernel
42	signature stays uniform). The host allocates ONLY the pointers the chosen
43	optimizer uses and zero-fills the rest; a stage dereferences only its own
44	optimizer's buffers. All FP32.
45	
46	| field | size (floats) | used by | meaning |
47	|-------|---------------|---------|---------|
48	| `prodigy_partials` | `2 * n_ctas` | prodigy | per-CTA (r,s) slots: `[0..n_ctas)`=r, `[n_ctas..2n_ctas)`=s |
49	| `prodigy_d` | `1` | prodigy | reduced d; bind `st.d_factor = prodigy_d[0]` |
50	| `muon_buf` | `rows*cols` | muon | momentum buffer (persists across steps) |
51	| `muon_X` | `rows*cols` | muon | current NS iterate |
52	| `muon_A` | `rows*rows` | muon | `A = X Xᵀ` |
53	| `muon_AX` | `rows*cols` | muon | `A X` |
54	| `muon_AAX` | `rows*cols` | muon | `A (A X)` |
55	| `muon_orth` | `rows*cols` | muon | NS output; bind `st.orth = muon_orth` |
56	| `muon_nrm_partials` | `n_ctas` | muon | per-CTA `‖buf‖_F²` slots |
57	| `muon_inv_norm` | `1` | muon | `1/(‖buf‖_F + 1e-7)` |
58	
59	`n_ctas == #SMs` (one persistent CTA per SM, `fused_megakernel.cuh:357`). The
60	muon matrix buffers are sized for the **largest** 2D weight processed (the stage
61	runs one matrix at a time; reuse the buffers across matrices).
62	
63	`prodigy_partials`, `muon_nrm_partials`, `prodigy_d`, `muon_inv_norm` must be
64	**zero-initialized before launch** (like the barrier counters,
65	`fused_megakernel.cuh:363-374`) — the owner-computes reducer reads every slot.
66	
67	---
68	
69	## 2. STAGED — prodigy (cross-ALL-tensors d, owner-computes tree)
70	
71	**Shape:** GLOBAL. One scalar `d` for the whole model; `r,s` sum over every
72	element of every parameter tensor.
73	
74	**Determinism deviation (contract-mandated, documented — not a transcription):**
75	the live per-op path reduces `r,s` with `atomicAdd` (`prodigy_sm90.cuh:105-108`,
76	`:135-138`). The COMPONENT_CONTRACT requires deterministic / no-float-atomic
77	reductions, so the stage REPLACES that with an owner-computes tree: each CTA
78	publishes its own `(r,s)` slot (no contention, no atomic) → grid barrier → one
79	owner thread sums the slots in ascending index order. Math-equivalent in exact
80	arithmetic; fp32 summation order is now fixed/reproducible.
81	
82	**Host/cell vs in-kernel split (faithful to the live multi-tensor driver):** the
83	PERSISTENT beta3-EMA decay of `(r,s)` across steps and the `d_coef` scaling live
84	in the host launcher (`prodigy_sm90.cuh:488-521`, `bindings.cpp:1246-1264`),
85	OUTSIDE `prodigy.h`. They are NOT in-kernel. The stage computes the INSTANTANEOUS
86	per-step `Σ r / Σ s` + `prodigy_update_d` (the cross-tensor reduction Audit-C
87	flagged). A cell that wants the grokking-race EMA estimator must, BETWEEN
88	phaseA-publish and phaseB-reduce: decay the prior `prodigy_partials` by `beta3`
89	and scale `r` by `d_coef` (host-side, on the workspace buffers) — exactly as the
90	live driver does around the same `prodigy_update_d`. The device math
91	(`prodigy.h`) stays byte-unchanged either way.
92	
93	**Codegen barrier sequence (per L3/L1 step):**
94	
95	```
96	// param_init = the Prodigy trajectory anchor (flat blob parallel to params).
97	optimizer_precompute_stage<Prodigy>(ctx, params, grad, sizes, offsets, st, ws,
98	                                    /*param_init=*/param_init);   // phaseA
99	bar.sync_reset(ctx.g_next_task);            // grid barrier; reset queue for reuse
100	prodigy_precompute_reduce_phaseB(ctx, st.d_factor, ws);          // owner-sum → d
101	bar.sync();                                  // d visible to all before apply
102	st.d_factor = ws.prodigy_d[0];               // bind the reduced d for the tail
103	// re-drain the queue for the apply (fused_optimizer_stage / the L3 bwd+opt):
104	apply_optimizer<Prodigy> over all tensors (opt_components.cuh:211-215).
105	```
106	
107	`st.d_factor` enters phaseA as `d_prev` (the comparison floor) and is OVERWRITTEN
108	post-reduce with the new `d`. Two grid barriers (reduce-publish, d-visible) plus
109	the queue resets — consistent with `fused_megakernel.cuh`'s phase pipeline.
110	
111	---
112	
113	## 3. STAGED — muon (Newton-Schulz orthogonalization, grid-cooperative)
114	
115	**Shape:** per-MATRIX, GRID-COOPERATIVE. A matmul is cross-element and a real 2D
116	weight does not fit one CTA's SMEM, so all CTAs cooperate on ONE matrix at a
117	time. This does NOT fit the flat one-CTA-per-tensor `(params, sizes, offsets)`
118	signature; the codegen drives the explicit phase fns (the
119	`optimizer_precompute_stage<Muon>` branch is a documented no-op that points
120	here).
121	
122	**New device code, cited:** the live path delegates `X Xᵀ`/`A X`/`A (A X)` to
123	`torch::mm`/cuBLAS (`bindings.cpp:992-994`), NOT a per-element canonical fn — so
124	the stage's tiled owner-computes matmul (`muon_matmul`) is legitimate new device
125	code, cited to that mm sequence. The drift guard requires only that the
126	ELEMENT-WISE pieces call `muon.h`: the momentum body and the NS polynomial
127	combine do (`muon_momentum_normalize_step` `muon.h:33-46`, `muon_ns_combine_step`
128	`muon.h:49-60`). The matmul contracts the k-dimension in ascending order (one
129	thread owns one output element) — deterministic fp32, no atomic.
130	
131	**1D params are NOT handled here** — they take the AdamW tail upstream
132	(`muon.h:75-76`, `bindings.cpp:970-977`). The codegen routes only 2D weights to
133	this stage.
134	
135	**Codegen sequence (per 2D matrix, `numel = rows*cols`, `ns_steps` default 5):**
136	
137	```
138	muon_momentum_norm_phaseA(grad_mtx, numel, momentum, ws);  // buf=μ·buf+g; ‖buf‖² slots
139	bar.sync();
140	muon_norm_reduce_phaseB(ctx, ws);                          // owner-sum → inv_norm
141	bar.sync();
142	muon_scale_X(numel, ws);                                   // X = buf*inv_norm (bindings.cpp:964)
143	bar.sync();
144	for (s = 0; s < ns_steps; ++s) {
145	    muon_matmul(ws.muon_X,  ws.muon_X, ws.muon_A,  rows, rows, cols, cols, cols, /*bT=*/true);  // A=XXᵀ
146	    bar.sync();
147	    muon_matmul(ws.muon_A,  ws.muon_X, ws.muon_AX, rows, cols, rows, rows, cols, /*bT=*/false); // AX
148	    bar.sync();
149	    muon_matmul(ws.muon_A,  ws.muon_AX,ws.muon_AAX,rows, cols, rows, rows, cols, /*bT=*/false); // A·AX
150	    bar.sync();
151	    muon_ns_combine_phase(numel, ws);                      // orth = a·X + b·AX + c·AAX
152	    bar.sync();
153	    std::swap(ws.muon_X, ws.muon_orth);  // next iter reads X; last iter result is in X
154	}
155	// After the loop the final orthogonalized matrix is in ws.muon_X (an odd # of
156	// swaps) — bind st.orth to whichever buffer holds the last combine output. With
157	// ns_steps swaps, the final result is in ws.muon_X iff ns_steps is even, else
158	// ws.muon_orth; the codegen tracks the parity (or copies into muon_orth once).
159	scale = 0.2f * sqrtf((float)max(rows, cols));   // bindings.cpp:981
160	st.orth         = <final NS buffer>;
161	st.neg_lr_scale = -lr * scale;                  // bindings.cpp:982
162	st.decay_factor = 1.0f - lr * wd;               // bindings.cpp:983
163	apply_optimizer<Muon> over this matrix (opt_components.cuh:230-234 → muon.h:63-73).
164	```

172	> orthogonalization inside ONE persistent megakernel is the heaviest stage; if a
173	> cell is register/SMEM-bound it may keep muon's NS as a SEPARATE launch (the L1
174	> tail still runs `apply_optimizer<Muon>` in-kernel reading `st.orth` produced by

181	## 4. STAGED — supergrok11 (meta-MLP mu + per-TENSOR cosine gate)
182	
183	**Shape: PER-TENSOR, SINGLE-DRAIN, NO grid barrier** — and the "no barrier" is
184	correct for a SUBTLE reason, NOT by analogy to anything. The live per-op path
185	(`bindings.cpp:1407-1416`) loops per parameter doing metanet→gate→adam, with each
186	tensor SELF-CONTAINED: `gate(T)` and `apply(T)` depend ONLY on `mu(T)`, never on
187	any other tensor's mu (`bindings.cpp:1411` computes the gate INSIDE the per-param
188	loop; `compute_cosine_gate_fused` takes ONE tensor's smart_grad/mu). So mu/gate/
189	apply for one tensor fuse into ONE body owned end-to-end by the SAME CTA inside
190	the codegen's existing single task-queue drain (`fused_optimizer_stage`,
191	`fused_megakernel.cuh:101-142`).
192	
193	> **Why NOT a separate full-queue mu pre-pass (the rejected Design A):** a mu
194	> stage that drains the queue to `n_tasks` and a SEPARATE apply drain would (a)
195	> need a grid barrier for cross-CTA mu visibility AND (b) **silently no-op** — the
196	> apply drain's `next_block()` returns `t >= n_tasks` immediately (the counter was
197	> consumed) and never applies, unless a `sync_reset` re-zeros it. The single-drain
198	> per-tensor form has NO such hazard. (Prodigy DOES use a barrier because its `d`
199	> is a genuine cross-ALL-tensors reduction — SG11's gate is per-tensor, so the
200	> cases are NOT analogous.)
201	
202	- **mu(T) — per ELEMENT**: `mu[i] = rescale · phi(grad[i], sharpness[i])` over the
203	  tensor slice (the meta-net is a per-TENSOR weight set).
204	- **gate(T) — per TENSOR**: block-level cosine tree over the SAME tensor's
205	  elements via the deterministic `block_reduce_sum_f32` (`primitives.cuh:125`) —
206	  no cross-CTA, no atomic.
207	
208	`sg11_precompute_mu_and_gate_for_tensor<32>` does BOTH (mu→`__syncthreads`→gate)
209	in one per-tensor call and RETURNS the gate; `sg_stage_phi_weights<32>` stages the
210	phi weights to SMEM once per block before the loop.
211	
212	**Gate formula — mirror the CODE not the stale comment.**
213	`compute_cosine_gate_fused` (`supergrok11_sm90.cuh:280-285`) computes
214	`clamp(<sg,mu> / sqrt(‖sg‖²·‖mu‖² + 1e-12), 0, 1)` with `sg == grad` (because
215	`bindings.cpp:1408` calls `mu_metanet` with `alpha=0`, so `smart_grad == grad`).
216	It **IGNORES** `gate_temp` despite the `bindings.cpp:1276` comment claiming
217	`sigmoid(t·cos)` — the function does a bare clamp, and `ref_sg11_step` agrees.
218	
219	**Codegen sequence (ONE task-queue drain; mu+gate+apply fused per tensor):**
220	
221	```
222	__shared__ float sW1[32*2], sb1[32], sW2[32];
223	sg_stage_phi_weights<32>(W1, b1, W2, sW1, sb1, sW2);   // once per block (syncs)
224	TaskQueue q = ctx.queue();
225	for (int t = q.next_block(&slot); t < ctx.n_tasks; t = q.next_block(&slot)) {
226	    int   n   = sizes[t];
227	    int64 off = offsets[t];
228	    // mu(T)→global, sync, gate(T) — SAME CTA owns T; reads the mu it just wrote.
229	    float gate = sg11_precompute_mu_and_gate_for_tensor<32>(
230	        st.mu, grad, sharpness, sW1, sb1, sW2, b2, rescale, off, n);
231	    FusedOptState ts = st;  ts.gate = gate;            // bind the per-tensor gate
232	    // apply over [off, off+n): the tail reads ts.mu + ts.gate.
233	    apply_optimizer<SuperGrok11> elementwise over the slice (opt_components.cuh:235-239).
234	}
235	```
236	No grid barrier, no `sync_reset` — one drain, race-free.
237	
238	> The apply (`sg11_sweep_b_step`, `supergrok11.h:79-111`) uses `smart_grad = g +
239	> (1-gate)*alpha*mu`. The live driver folds `ramp*lamb` into a `lamb_eff`
240	> multiplier (`bindings.cpp:1400-1416`); if a cell needs that, it sets
241	> `st.alpha = ramp*lamb*alpha` (the apply's `alpha` slot) so the single live
242	> correction matches — a scalar binding, no math change.
243	
244	### ⚠ ABI GAP — `sharpness` is not in `FusedOptState` (flag loudly)
245	
246	`sharpness` is **model-coupled**, exactly like looksam's `sam_dir`: it is
247	`(sam_grad − normal_grad)²` from a SAM SECOND backward
248	(`sg11_sharpness_restore_kernel`, `supergrok11_sm90.cuh:236-248`).
249	`FusedOptState` (`opt_components.cuh:84-113`, which the stage header MUST NOT
250	edit) has a `mu` field but **NO `sharpness` field and NO phi-weight fields**.
251	Therefore the stage takes `sharpness` + `(W1,b1,W2,b2,rescale)` as **explicit
252	pointers/scalars**, and the cell must supply a sharpness buffer the current ABI
253	does not carry. Two integration options (a sibling agent owning `opt_components
254	.cuh` chooses):
255	
256	1. **Extend the ABI** (preferred long-term): add `const float* sharpness` and the
257	   phi-weight pointers to `FusedOptState`, populated by the cell like the other
258	   model-coupled inputs. Requires editing `opt_components.cuh` (out of THIS
259	   phase's scope).
260	2. **Side-channel pointers** (no ABI change): the cell passes `sharpness` + phi
261	   weights as extra kernel arguments straight into
262	   `sg11_precompute_mu_and_gate_for_tensor<32>` / `sg15_precompute_mu_for_tensor
263	   <32>` (their signatures take them explicitly). The codegen threads them
264	   alongside `FusedOptState`.
265	
266	Until one is wired, an SG11/SG15 cell CANNOT run fully in-kernel — the
267	sharpness pipeline (SAM perturb → 2nd backward → restore) is a model-stage
268	responsibility documented here, not faked in the optimizer stage.
269

272	## 5. STAGED — supergrok15 (meta-MLP mu; gate is a host scalar)
273	
274	Same PER-TENSOR single-drain shape as SG11 — but SIMPLER: NO gate stage at all
275	(the phi-net shares the SG11/SG15 form, `supergrok15.h:34-52`). DIFFERENCES:
276	
277	- **gate is GLOBAL = sigmoid(training accuracy)**, set HOST-side and passed as a
278	  scalar (`supergrok15.h:85`), already carried by `FusedScalars.gate`
279	  (`opt_components.cuh:153`). **No gate reduction stage, no per-tensor gate.**
280	- the per-coord alpha clip (`sg15_alpha_per_coord`, `supergrok15.h:68-75`) and
281	  `smart_grad = g + gate*a*mu` happen INSIDE the apply tail
282	  (`apply_optimizer<SuperGrok15>` → `sg15_sweep_b_step`,
283	  `opt_components.cuh:240-244`). So the ONLY precompute is `mu`.
284	- `sg15_sweep_a` also accumulates a `sharpness²` partial
285	  (`supergrok15_sm90.cuh:99-102`) that updates the NEXT step's `sharpness` input
286	  host-side; it is NOT consumed by THIS step's apply (which reads `mu` + the host
287	  gate). It is part of the model-coupled sharpness pipeline, documented here,
288	  not computed in this step's optimizer precompute.
289	
290	**Codegen sequence (ONE drain; mu+apply fused per tensor, no gate, no barrier):**
291

293	__shared__ float sW1[32*2], sb1[32], sW2[32];
294	sg_stage_phi_weights<32>(W1, b1, W2, sW1, sb1, sW2);   // once per block (syncs)
295	st.gate = sigmoid(accuracy);     // host scalar (FusedScalars.gate) — NO stage
296	TaskQueue q = ctx.queue();
297	for (int t = q.next_block(&slot); t < ctx.n_tasks; t = q.next_block(&slot)) {
298	    int n = sizes[t];  int64 off = offsets[t];
299	    sg15_precompute_mu_for_tensor<32>(st.mu, grad, sharpness,
300	                                      sW1, sb1, sW2, b2, rescale, off, n);
301	    __syncthreads();   // mu(T) visible before the apply reads it (block-scope)
302	    apply_optimizer<SuperGrok15> over [off, off+n) (opt_components.cuh:240-244).
303	}
304	```
305	One drain, no grid barrier, no `sync_reset`.

312	## 6. MODEL-COUPLED — looksam (`st.sam_dir` from the model stage)
313	
314	`looksam_apply_step` (`looksam.h:63-91`) reads `st.sam_dir`. On a SAM step
315	`sam_dir = g_sam − g` (`looksam.h:52-59`) where `g_sam` is the gradient at the
316	PERTURBED weights `p + rho·g/‖g‖` (`looksam.h:27-38`) — the output of a SECOND
317	model backward. A pure optimizer stage cannot produce it. There is therefore NO
318	looksam specialization of `optimizer_precompute_stage` by design.
319	
320	**Contract:** the MODEL STAGE fills `st.sam_dir` on SAM steps (every k steps),
321	mirroring the per-op LookSAM pipeline (perturb → 2nd backward → `set_direction`).
322	On intervening steps the cached `sam_dir` is reused verbatim (`looksam.h:1-19`).
323	`FusedOptState.sam_dir` (`opt_components.cuh:91`) already exists as the bound
324	input; the cell points it at the model-produced buffer. The wiring of the SAM
325	second backward into the megakernel's model phase is the model-stage owner's
326	responsibility (out of THIS phase's scope), tracked here as the explicit
327	contract so it is not silently dropped.
328

331	## 7. Determinism summary (no float atomics anywhere)
332	
333	| stage | reduction | determinism mechanism |
334	|-------|-----------|------------------------|
335	| prodigy d | cross-all-tensors `(r,s)` | per-CTA slot publish → barrier → ascending-index owner-sum (`owner_sum_slots`) |
336	| muon ‖buf‖_F | cross-CTA over one matrix | per-CTA slot publish → barrier → ascending owner-sum |

338	| sg11 cosine gate | per-tensor `(num, den_g, den_m)` | in-CTA `block_reduce_sum_f32` tree (fixed thread count) |
339	
340	No `atomicAdd` on floats anywhere in `opt_stages_precompute.cuh`. The only
341	atomics are the substrate's integer task-counter and barrier-generation
342	(`megakernel_common.cuh`), which are order-independent.

2	// SuperGrok v1.1 — vendor-neutral algorithm header.
3	//
4	// Reference: internal algorithm. The Python source of truth is
5	// `grokking_optimizers/optimizers/supergrok11.py` — this header
6	// reproduces the per-parameter math from `_single_param_step` and the
7	// batched fused-kernel logic from supergrok11_fused_step.
8	//
9	// Element-wise MLP gradient transformation with cosine-similarity gating.
10	// Same structure as v1.5 but the gating term is the cosine between grad
11	// and momentum (computed per-parameter), not a sigmoid of training accuracy.
12	//
13	// Calling convention: bc1, bc2 are passed un-inverted —
14	//   bc1 = 1 - beta1^t,  bc2 = 1 - beta2^t.
15	//
16	// Pipeline per step (two cooperative sweeps):
17	//
18	//   Sweep A — meta-net forward:
19	//     mu = mlp_phi(grad, sharpness)
20	//     gate_num += grad * momentum
21	//     gate_den_g += grad * grad
22	//     gate_den_m += momentum * momentum
23	//
24	//   Sweep B — apply:
25	//     gate = clamp(gate_num / sqrt(gate_den_g * gate_den_m + eps), 0, 1)
26	//     smart_grad = grad + (1 - gate) * alpha * mu
27	//     AdamW step on smart_grad with trust-ratio scaling.
28	
29	#include "csrc/common/types.h"
30	#include "csrc/common/utils.cuh"
31	
32	namespace sg { namespace algorithms {
33	
34	// MLP forward: GELU hidden, linear output (matches the canonical trainable
35	// PyTorch SharpnessMetaNet, which uses nn.GELU). Phi weights: W1[H,2], b1[H],
36	// W2[H], b2.
37	template <int H>
38	__device__ __forceinline__ float sg11_phi_forward(
39	    const float grad_val,
40	    const float sharp_val,
41	    const float* __restrict__ W1,
42	    const float* __restrict__ b1,
43	    const float* __restrict__ W2,
44	    const float b2
45	) {
46	    float h_acc = 0.0f;
47	    #pragma unroll
48	    for (int j = 0; j < H; j++) {
49	        float h = W1[j * 2] * grad_val + W1[j * 2 + 1] * sharp_val + b1[j];
50	        // Exact erf GELU — matches torch.nn.GELU() in the trainable meta-net.
51	        h = 0.5f * h * (1.0f + erff(h * 0.70710678118654752f));
52	        h_acc += W2[j] * h;
53	    }
54	    return h_acc + b2;
55	}
56	
57	// Sweep A per-element: compute mu and contribute to cosine reductions.
58	template <typename GradT>
59	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg11_sweep_a_step(
60	    float* __restrict__ mu_out,
61	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad,
62	    const float* __restrict__ sharpness,
63	    const float* __restrict__ momentum,
64	    const float mu_val,
65	    const int64_t idx,
66	    float& gate_num_local,
67	    float& gate_den_g_local,
68	    float& gate_den_m_local
69	) {
70	    mu_out[idx] = mu_val;
71	    const float g = static_cast<float>(grad[idx]);
72	    const float m = momentum[idx];
73	    gate_num_local   += g * m;
74	    gate_den_g_local += g * g;
75	    gate_den_m_local += m * m;
76	}
77	
78	// Sweep B per-element: cosine gate + smart_grad + Adam.
79	template <typename ParamT, typename GradT>
80	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg11_sweep_b_step(
81	    ParamT* __restrict__ param,
82	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg,
83	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg_sq,
84	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad,
85	    const float* __restrict__ mu,
86	    const float gate,            // pre-reduced cosine similarity, clamped
87	    const float alpha,           // meta-net strength
88	    const float lr,
89	    const float beta1,
90	    const float beta2,
91	    const float eps,
92	    const float wd,
93	    const float bc1,
94	    const float bc2,
95	    const int64_t idx
96	) {
97	    const float g  = static_cast<float>(grad[idx]);
98	    const float p  = static_cast<float>(param[idx]);
99	    const float u  = mu[idx];
100	
101	    const float smart_grad = g + (1.0f - gate) * alpha * u;
102	
103	    const float m = beta1 * exp_avg[idx]    + (1.0f - beta1) * smart_grad;
104	    const float v = beta2 * exp_avg_sq[idx] + (1.0f - beta2) * smart_grad * smart_grad;
105	    exp_avg[idx]    = m;
106	    exp_avg_sq[idx] = v;
107	
108	    // bc1, bc2 un-inverted (= 1 - beta^t): divide for bias correction.
109	    const float update = (m / sg_safe_bc(bc1)) / (sqrtf(v / sg_safe_bc(bc2)) + eps);
110	    param[idx] = static_cast<ParamT>(p - lr * (update + wd * p));
111	}
112	
113	// Canonical bias-corrected Adam tail on a caller-supplied effective gradient
114	// g_eff. SINGLE source of the moment-update + decoupled-WD apply math, factored
115	// out of sg11_sweep_b_step so the decoupled "Adam-on (smart_grad + lamb_eff*mu)"
116	// kernel can reuse the exact same float ops without re-inlining them. The
117	// caller computes its optimizer-specific g_eff; this writes the new moments
118	// into exp_avg[idx]/exp_avg_sq[idx] and the new parameter into param[idx].
119	//
120	// Bit-identical to the tail of sg11_sweep_b_step:
121	//   m = beta1 * exp_avg[idx]    + (1 - beta1) * g_eff;
122	//   v = beta2 * exp_avg_sq[idx] + (1 - beta2) * g_eff * g_eff;
123	//   update = (m / bc1) / (sqrtf(v / bc2) + eps);
124	//   param[idx] = p - lr * (update + wd * p);
125	template <typename ParamT>
126	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg11_adam_tail(
127	    ParamT* __restrict__ param,
128	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg,
129	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg_sq,
130	    const float g_eff,
131	    const float lr,
132	    const float beta1,
133	    const float beta2,
134	    const float eps,
135	    const float wd,
136	    const float bc1,
137	    const float bc2,
138	    const int64_t idx
139	) {
140	    const float p = static_cast<float>(param[idx]);
141	    const float m = beta1 * exp_avg[idx]    + (1.0f - beta1) * g_eff;
142	    const float v = beta2 * exp_avg_sq[idx] + (1.0f - beta2) * g_eff * g_eff;
143	    exp_avg[idx]    = m;

1	#pragma once
2	// SuperGrok v1.5 — vendor-neutral algorithm header.
3	//
4	// Reference: internal algorithm. The Python source of truth is
5	// `grokking_optimizers/optimizers/supergrok15.py` — this header
6	// reproduces the per-parameter math from `_single_param_step` and the
7	// batched fused-kernel logic from supergrok15_fused_step.
8	//
9	// Element-wise MLP gradient transformation with sigmoid gating on training
10	// accuracy. Same structure as v1.1 but the gate is a scalar sigmoid of
11	// accuracy (set host-side), not a per-parameter cosine.
12	//
13	// Calling convention: bc1, bc2 are passed un-inverted —
14	//   bc1 = 1 - beta1^t,  bc2 = 1 - beta2^t.
15	//
16	// Pipeline per step:
17	//
18	//   Sweep A — meta-net forward + sharpness reduction:
19	//     mu = mlp_phi(grad, sharpness)
20	//     sharpness_sum += grad - grad_prev   (used to update sharpness)
21	//
22	//   Sweep B — apply:
23	//     alpha_per_coord clipped to [0, 1]
24	//     smart_grad = grad + alpha * mu
25	//     AdamW step on smart_grad.
26	
27	#include "csrc/common/types.h"
28	#include "csrc/common/utils.cuh"
29	
30	namespace sg { namespace algorithms {
31	
32	// MLP forward: same shape as v1.1 (GELU hidden, linear output — matches the
33	// trainable PyTorch SharpnessMetaNet's nn.GELU).
34	template <int H>
35	__device__ __forceinline__ float sg15_phi_forward(
36	    const float grad_val,
37	    const float sharp_val,
38	    const float* __restrict__ W1,
39	    const float* __restrict__ b1,
40	    const float* __restrict__ W2,
41	    const float b2
42	) {
43	    float h_acc = 0.0f;
44	    #pragma unroll
45	    for (int j = 0; j < H; j++) {
46	        float h = W1[j * 2] * grad_val + W1[j * 2 + 1] * sharp_val + b1[j];
47	        // Exact erf GELU — matches torch.nn.GELU() in the trainable meta-net.
48	        h = 0.5f * h * (1.0f + erff(h * 0.70710678118654752f));
49	        h_acc += W2[j] * h;
50	    }
51	    return h_acc + b2;
52	}
53	
54	// Sweep A: compute mu and write back; contribute to sharpness reduction.
55	template <typename GradT>
56	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg15_sweep_a_step(
57	    float* __restrict__ mu_out,
58	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad,
59	    const float mu_val,
60	    const int64_t idx,
61	    float& sharp_local
62	) {
63	    mu_out[idx] = mu_val;
64	    sharp_local += static_cast<float>(grad[idx]) * static_cast<float>(grad[idx]);
65	}
66	
67	// Per-coord alpha gate: clipped affine of mu.
68	__device__ __forceinline__ float sg15_alpha_per_coord(
69	    const float mu_val,
70	    const float alpha_base,
71	    const float alpha_max
72	) {
73	    const float a = alpha_base * (1.0f + mu_val);
74	    return fminf(fmaxf(a, 0.0f), alpha_max);
75	}
76	
77	// Sweep B: smart_grad + Adam, register-resident.
78	template <typename ParamT, typename GradT>
79	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg15_sweep_b_step(
80	    ParamT* __restrict__ param,
81	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg,
82	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg_sq,
83	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad,
84	    const float* __restrict__ mu,
85	    const float gate_global,     // sigmoid(accuracy)
86	    const float alpha_base,
87	    const float alpha_max,
88	    const float lr,
89	    const float beta1,
90	    const float beta2,
91	    const float eps,
92	    const float wd,
93	    const float bc1,
94	    const float bc2,
95	    const int64_t idx
96	) {
97	    const float g = static_cast<float>(grad[idx]);
98	    const float p = static_cast<float>(param[idx]);
99	    const float u = mu[idx];
100	
101	    const float a = sg15_alpha_per_coord(u, alpha_base, alpha_max);
102	    const float smart_grad = g + gate_global * a * u;
103	
104	    const float m = beta1 * exp_avg[idx]    + (1.0f - beta1) * smart_grad;
105	    const float v = beta2 * exp_avg_sq[idx] + (1.0f - beta2) * smart_grad * smart_grad;
106	    exp_avg[idx]    = m;
107	    exp_avg_sq[idx] = v;
108	
109	    // bc1, bc2 un-inverted (= 1 - beta^t): divide for bias correction.
110	    const float update = (m / sg_safe_bc(bc1)) / (sqrtf(v / sg_safe_bc(bc2)) + eps);
111	    param[idx] = static_cast<ParamT>(p - lr * (update + wd * p));
112	}
113	
114	}} // namespace sg::algorithms

1	#ifndef SG_FUSED_SM90_OPT_COMPONENTS_CUH_
2	#define SG_FUSED_SM90_OPT_COMPONENTS_CUH_
3	// ============================================================================
4	// csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_components.cuh — REAL per-optimizer device-function
5	// composition library for the sm_90 fused L3 megakernel (Phase 3 Stage 5).
6	//
7	// THIS REPLACES THE FALSE POSITIVE. The previous fused path (megakernel_demo.cu
8	// :opt_update<Opt>) implemented only 4 optimizers (AdamW/Lion/Muon/SuperGrok15)
9	// with TOY math, and the codegen mapped the other 7 to the AdamW tail — i.e.
10	// `mega_*_prodigy.cu` actually ran AdamW. That is the breadth-faking this stage
11	// eliminates.
12	//
13	// Here every one of the 11 optimizers calls its OWN, REAL per-element update
14	// function from csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h (the canonical optimizer component —
15	// the same device functions the per-op launchers compile). No fallback, no
16	// templating one optimizer from another, no toy substitute. Each optimizer's
17	// genuine state buffers are plumbed through FusedOptState.
18	//
19	// SCOPE / HONESTY (the fused TAIL vs the outer loop):
20	//   The L3 megakernel fuses the per-element optimizer TAIL after fwd+bwd. The
21	//   multi-phase OUTER parts that are not per-element — Muon's Newton–Schulz
22	//   orthogonalization, Prodigy's global d reduction, LookSAM's perturb/restore
23	//   ascent, SG11/SG15's cosine-gate reduction, and SG2's CSA/HCA+PEER meta-net
24	//   — run as their own launch(es) and hand this tail the precomputed result
25	//   (orth direction, d factor, sam_dir, reduced gate, smart-grad). This mirrors
26	//   the real per-op pipelines exactly; the tail math below IS the real apply.
27	// ============================================================================
28	
29	#include <cuda_runtime.h>
30	#include <cstdint>
31	
32	// The 11 canonical optimizer components (real per-element device functions).
33	#include "csrc/algorithms/adamw.h"
34	#include "csrc/algorithms/lion.h"
35	#include "csrc/algorithms/grokfast.h"
36	#include "csrc/algorithms/grokadamw.h"
37	#include "csrc/algorithms/looksam.h"
38	#include "csrc/algorithms/prodigy.h"
39	#include "csrc/algorithms/neuralgrok.h"
40	#include "csrc/algorithms/muon.h"
41	#include "csrc/algorithms/supergrok11.h"
42	#include "csrc/algorithms/supergrok15.h"
43	// SG2's elementwise tail is an Adam apply on the meta-net smart-grad; the
44	// metanet itself (supergrok2.h / supergrok2_bilevel_adjoint.h) is the separate
45	// CSA/HCA launch. adamw.h already pulled in above covers the tail.
46	
47	namespace sg { namespace fused { namespace sm90 {
48	
49	namespace algo = ::sg::algorithms;
50	
51	// Compile-time optimizer selector — one value per real optimizer (no aliases,
52	// no fallback). Must match grokking_optimizers/megakernel_codegen.py's set.
53	enum class OptId : int {
54	    AdamW = 0, Lion = 1, Grokfast = 2, GrokAdamW = 3, LookSAM = 4,
55	    Prodigy = 5, NeuralGrok = 6, Muon = 7, SuperGrok11 = 8,
56	    SuperGrok15 = 9, SuperGrok2 = 10
57	};
58	
59	// NeuralGrok / SG11 / SG15 psi/phi MLP hidden width (compile-time). Matches the
60	// per-op neuralgrok kernel's default instantiation.
61	static constexpr int kPsiHidden = 16;
62	
63	// #5 — NeuralGrok psi-net weight packing in the cell's `extra` buffer.
64	// neuralgrok has no per-element `extra` n-slice (its psi-net is a small
65	// per-TENSOR weight set), so the cell repurposes the otherwise-unused `extra`
66	// pointer to carry the packed psi-net weights in this fixed layout:
67	//   extra[0                  .. kPsiHidden)        = psi_W1  [kPsiHidden]
68	//   extra[kPsiHidden         .. 2*kPsiHidden)      = psi_b1  [kPsiHidden]
69	//   extra[2*kPsiHidden       .. 3*kPsiHidden)      = psi_W2  [kPsiHidden]
70	//   extra[3*kPsiHidden]                            = psi_b2  (scalar)
71	// A neuralgrok cell binds st.psi_W1/b1/W2 from these offsets so the device read
72	// of the psi weights is a real, bound pointer instead of a null-deref. psi_b2
73	// is a device scalar; the cell leaves st.psi_b2 at its 0.0f default (a host
74	// scalar cannot dereference a device pointer) — see the #5 stop in the report.
75	static constexpr int kPsiW1Off = 0;
76	static constexpr int kPsiB1Off = kPsiHidden;
77	static constexpr int kPsiW2Off = 2 * kPsiHidden;
78	static constexpr int kPsiB2Off = 3 * kPsiHidden;   // scalar slot (device-side)
79	static constexpr int kPsiPackFloats = 3 * kPsiHidden + 1;
80	
81	// All optimizer state any of the 11 tails may read. A given cell zero-fills the
82	// pointers its optimizer does not use; each apply_optimizer<> branch touches
83	// ONLY its own optimizer's real buffers (so unused ones are never dereferenced).
84	struct FusedOptState {
85	    // Adam-family moments (shared by almost all).
86	    float* exp_avg     = nullptr;   // m
87	    float* exp_avg_sq  = nullptr;   // v
88	    // Grokfast / GrokAdamW slow-gradient EMA.
89	    float* ema         = nullptr;
90	    // LookSAM precomputed SAM ascent direction.
91	    const float* sam_dir = nullptr;
92	    // Prodigy trajectory accumulator + adaptive d (scalar, host/reduce-stage).
93	    float* s_track     = nullptr;
94	    float  d_factor    = 1.0f;
95	    // SG11/SG15 momentum buffer + reduced cosine/accuracy gate (scalar).
96	    float* mu          = nullptr;
97	    float  gate        = 1.0f;
98	    // Muon precomputed Newton–Schulz orthogonalized direction + step scales.
99	    const float* orth  = nullptr;
100	    float  neg_lr_scale = 0.0f;
101	    float  decay_factor = 1.0f;
102	    // NeuralGrok psi-net (per-tensor MLP weights) — psi computed per element.
103	    const float* psi_W1 = nullptr;   // [kPsiHidden]
104	    const float* psi_b1 = nullptr;   // [kPsiHidden]
105	    const float* psi_W2 = nullptr;   // [kPsiHidden]
106	    float        psi_b2 = 0.0f;
107	    // SG2 smart-grad from the CSA/HCA meta-net launch (drives the Adam tail).
108	    const float* smart_grad = nullptr;
109	    // Shared hyperparameters.
110	    float lr = 1e-3f, beta1 = 0.9f, beta2 = 0.999f, eps = 1e-8f, wd = 0.01f;
111	    float bc1 = 1.0f, bc2 = 1.0f;       // un-inverted bias-corrections
112	    float alpha = 0.98f, beta = 0.0f, lamb = 2.0f, alpha_max = 1.0f;
113	    // GrokAdamW (decoder L3-TC conversion): layer-wise β1 decay rate γ + global
114	    // grad-norm clip threshold. clip_coef is DEVICE-computed once per launch (the
115	    // global grad-norm reduction in P2.5) and stashed here; it passes through
116	    // rebase_state unchanged (a scalar). Defaults are the inert no-op (γ=0 ⇒ a
117	    // single global β1; grad_clip<=0 ⇒ no clip; clip_coef=1 ⇒ grad unscaled).
118	    float gamma = 0.0f, grad_clip = 0.0f, clip_coef = 1.0f;
119	    // Prodigy (decoder L3-TC conversion, STAGED global-d). The d-estimate's
120	    // INPUTS that the in-kernel reduction stage (fused_decoder_megakernel_tc's
121	    // Prodigy branch, between B2 and P3) consumes/produces:
122	    //   * param_init — the trajectory anchor p0 (flat blob parallel to params),
123	    //     seeded = params at step 1 by the host; r = Σ d²·<g, p0−p> needs it.
124	    //     rebase_state offsets it per tensor (added below).
125	    //   * d0 / d_coef / beta3 — the estimator scalars (host-bound via FusedScalars):
126	    //     d0 seeds d_prev at step 1 (the persisted d_lr slot zero-inits to 0, but
127	    //     eager inits _d_lr=d0=1e-6 — the cold-start the single-step gate needs);
128	    //     beta3=sqrt(β2) decays the persistent (r_ema,s_ema); d_coef scales the
129	    //     candidate d. Defaults are the inert/eager values (d_coef=1 ⇒ no scale).
130	    //   * prodigy_persist — device pointer to the 3 PERSISTED estimator scalars
131	    //     [r_ema | s_ema | d_lr] that carry across steps (host owns the buffer; the
132	    //     stage decays + accumulates + writes d back each step). NOT rebased.
133	    // st.s_track (Prodigy's `s` buffer) + st.d_factor (the reduced d the apply
134	    // reads) already exist above. Defaults leave every non-Prodigy cell untouched.
135	    const float* param_init = nullptr;
136	    float* prodigy_persist  = nullptr;   // [r_ema | s_ema | d_lr]  (persisted)
137	    float d0 = 1e-6f, d_coef = 1.0f, beta3 = 0.0f;
138	    // Muon (ViT L3-TC, STAGED NS): the 1D-weight AdamW group's INDEPENDENT
139	    // hyperparameters (eager adamw_lr/adamw_betas, muon.py:115-125). The 2D group's
140	    // lr/momentum ride the main lr/beta1 fields (P2.7 NS + apply); the 1D AdamW
141	    // tail (P3) reads aux_lr/aux_beta1/aux_beta2 instead (bc1/bc2 device-computed
142	    // = 1-aux_beta^step). Defaults = eager Muon adamw_* defaults; non-Muon cells
143	    // never read these (byte-identical).
144	    float aux_lr = 1e-3f, aux_beta1 = 0.9f, aux_beta2 = 0.98f;
145	    // LookSAM (decoder/vit/mamba L3-TC, MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd backward). rho is the
146	    // perturbation radius; the model phase computes rho_over_norm = rho/‖g‖_global
147	    // ON-DEVICE (same deterministic ascending-CTA reduction as GrokAdamW's P2.5),
148	    // perturbs p'=p+rho_over_norm·g, runs a SECOND in-kernel fwd+bwd at p' → g_sam,
149	    // and writes st.sam_dir = g_sam − g (persisted in the `extra` state slice) BEFORE
150	    // the apply tail blends g_adj=(1−α)g+α·sam_dir. looksam_sam is the SAM-step gate
151	    // (1.0 on every-k SAM steps, 0.0 on intervening steps — the host computes it from
152	    // the optimizer's _global_step%%k cadence); when 0 the cached sam_dir is reused
153	    // verbatim and NO 2nd backward runs. α rides the shared st.alpha field. Defaults
154	    // are inert (rho=0 ⇒ no perturb; looksam_sam=0 ⇒ no 2nd pass) so every non-LookSAM
155	    // cell is byte-identical.
156	    float rho = 0.0f, looksam_sam = 0.0f;
157	};
158	
159	// =========================================================================
160	//  FusedScalars — the FULL runtime scalar set the host passes per fused_step.
161	//
162	//  C2-GAP FIX (the whole point of this struct). Previously each mega_*.cu host
163	//  entry bound ONLY pointers + lr into FusedOptState and left every other scalar
164	//  at its struct default — which silently froze the math: bc1/bc2 == 1.0 (NO
165	//  Adam bias correction, stuck at t=1), gate == 1.0 (SG gating inert), d_factor
166	//  == 1.0 (Prodigy d-adaptation inert), and beta1/beta2/eps/wd/alpha/lamb/
167	//  alpha_max/beta/neg_lr_scale/decay_factor never reaching apply_optimizer<>.
168	//  apply_optimizer<> already READS all of these from FusedOptState; the only gap
169	//  was that nobody SET them. This POD carries them across the host→kernel ABI so
170	//  the cell can populate FusedOptState with the live optimizer's real values.
171	//
172	//  Defaults here reproduce the OLD inert behavior EXACTLY (bc=gate=d_factor=1,
173	//  decay_factor=1, the same beta/eps/wd/alpha defaults), so a caller that does
174	//  not pass scalars yields byte-identical results to the pre-fix cells — the
175	//  widening is additive, not a behavior change for unset fields.
176	//
177	//  Per-tensor step count / bias correction (loud assumption): the megakernel
178	//  treats the whole flat param as ONE task, so a SINGLE (bc1, bc2) pair is bound
179	//  per call. That is correct ONLY when every parameter tensor shares the same
180	//  step counter — which holds in the grokking race (all params step together
181	//  every iteration). The host computes bc1 = 1 - beta1^step, bc2 = 1 - beta2^step
182	//  from that shared step and passes them here. If a future caller steps tensors
183	//  at different counts, it must call fused_step per-tensor with that tensor's bc.
184	// =========================================================================
185	struct FusedScalars {
186	    float lr           = 1e-3f;
187	    float beta1        = 0.9f;
188	    float beta2        = 0.999f;
189	    float eps          = 1e-8f;
190	    float wd           = 0.01f;
191	    float bc1          = 1.0f;   // 1 - beta1^step (un-inverted; apply divides)
192	    float bc2          = 1.0f;   // 1 - beta2^step (un-inverted; apply divides)
193	    float alpha        = 0.98f;  // meta-net strength / grokfast_alpha / neuralgrok alpha
194	    float beta         = 0.0f;   // neuralgrok beta (affine psi term)
195	    float lamb         = 2.0f;   // grokfast/grokadamw amplification (grokfast_lamb)
196	    float alpha_max    = 1.0f;   // SG15 per-coord alpha clip ceiling
197	    float gate         = 1.0f;   // SG11 cosine gate / SG15 sigmoid(accuracy) gate
198	    float d_factor     = 1.0f;   // Prodigy adaptive d (effective LR scale)
199	    float neg_lr_scale = 0.0f;   // Muon: -lr * ns_scale (2D NS-orth apply)
200	    float decay_factor = 1.0f;   // Muon: 1 - lr*wd (decoupled decay multiplier)
201	    // ── GrokAdamW append-only widening (decoder L3-TC conversion). Both default
202	    //    to the INERT value (0.0 ⇒ disabled), so every other cell is byte-identical
203	    //    (additive ABI, same contract as the original C2-gap widening above).
204	    float gamma     = 0.0f;   // GrokAdamW layer-wise β1 decay rate: β1_i=β1*(1-γ)^i
205	    float grad_clip = 0.0f;   // GrokAdamW global grad-norm clip (<=0 ⇒ no clip)
206	    // ── Prodigy append-only widening (decoder L3-TC conversion, STAGED global-d).
207	    //    The estimator scalars; defaults are eager/inert so every other cell is
208	    //    byte-identical. d0 seeds d_prev at step 1; beta3=sqrt(β2) decays the
209	    //    persisted (r_ema,s_ema); d_coef scales the candidate d (1 ⇒ no scale).
210	    float d0     = 1e-6f;     // Prodigy d0 (step-1 d_prev cold-start)
211	    float d_coef = 1.0f;      // Prodigy d_coef (candidate-d scale)
212	    float beta3  = 0.0f;      // Prodigy EMA decay = sqrt(beta2) (0 ⇒ no persistence)
213	    // ── Muon append-only widening (ViT L3-TC, STAGED NS). The eager Muon manages
214	    //    TWO param groups with INDEPENDENT hyperparameters: a 2D-matrix group
215	    //    (lr/momentum carried by the main lr/beta1 fields, consumed by the P2.7 NS
216	    //    + apply) and a 1D-weight AdamW group (muon.py:115-125: adamw_lr,
217	    //    adamw_betas, shared weight_decay). A single global scalar set cannot map
218	    //    the main lr/beta1 onto BOTH groups, so the 1D AdamW tail (P3) reads these
219	    //    aux_* fields instead. aux_bc1/bc2 are NOT carried — the muon branch
220	    //    computes them on-device (1-aux_beta^step), shrinking the mirror surface.
221	    //    Defaults mirror the eager Muon adamw_* defaults; every non-Muon caller is
222	    //    byte-identical (only the OptId::Muon P3 branch reads aux_*).
223	    float aux_lr    = 1e-3f;  // Muon 1D-group AdamW lr (eager adamw_lr)
224	    float aux_beta1 = 0.9f;   // Muon 1D-group AdamW betas[0] (eager adamw_betas[0])
225	    float aux_beta2 = 0.98f;  // Muon 1D-group AdamW betas[1] (eager adamw_betas[1])
226	    // ── LookSAM append-only widening (decoder/vit/mamba L3-TC, MODEL-COUPLED SAM
227	    //    2nd backward). rho = SAM perturbation radius; looksam_sam = the every-k
228	    //    SAM-step gate (1.0 ⇒ run the in-kernel perturb→2nd fwd+bwd→sam_dir=g_sam−g;
229	    //    0.0 ⇒ reuse the cached sam_dir, no 2nd pass). α rides the existing `alpha`
230	    //    field. Defaults are inert (rho=0 / looksam_sam=0), so every non-LookSAM
231	    //    caller is byte-identical (only OptId::LookSAM's model phase reads them).
232	    float rho         = 0.0f;
233	    float looksam_sam = 0.0f;
234	};
235	
236	// Fold the runtime scalars into a FusedOptState (pointers are bound separately
237	// by each cell). Single seam so every cell applies the SAME scalar mapping — no
238	// per-cell drift in which field a scalar lands in. apply_optimizer<> reads these
239	// exact fields, so this is the bridge that un-freezes bc1/bc2/gate/d_factor/etc.
240	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ void apply_scalars(FusedOptState& st,
241	                                                        const FusedScalars& s) {
242	    st.lr           = s.lr;
243	    st.beta1        = s.beta1;
244	    st.beta2        = s.beta2;
245	    st.eps          = s.eps;
246	    st.wd           = s.wd;
247	    st.bc1          = s.bc1;
248	    st.bc2          = s.bc2;
249	    st.alpha        = s.alpha;
250	    st.beta         = s.beta;
251	    st.lamb         = s.lamb;
252	    st.alpha_max    = s.alpha_max;
253	    st.gate         = s.gate;
254	    st.d_factor     = s.d_factor;
255	    st.neg_lr_scale = s.neg_lr_scale;
256	    st.decay_factor = s.decay_factor;
257	    st.gamma        = s.gamma;       // GrokAdamW layer-wise β1 decay rate
258	    st.grad_clip    = s.grad_clip;   // GrokAdamW global grad-norm clip threshold
259	    // st.clip_coef is NOT host-bound: the kernel computes it on-device (P2.5) from
260	    // the reduced grad's global L2 norm and st.grad_clip, then applies it in P3.
261	    st.d0           = s.d0;          // Prodigy d0 (step-1 d_prev cold-start)
262	    st.d_coef       = s.d_coef;      // Prodigy candidate-d scale
263	    st.beta3        = s.beta3;       // Prodigy EMA decay (sqrt(beta2))
264	    st.aux_lr       = s.aux_lr;      // Muon 1D-group AdamW lr (eager adamw_lr)
265	    st.aux_beta1    = s.aux_beta1;   // Muon 1D-group AdamW betas[0]
266	    st.aux_beta2    = s.aux_beta2;   // Muon 1D-group AdamW betas[1]
267	    st.rho          = s.rho;         // LookSAM perturbation radius
268	    st.looksam_sam  = s.looksam_sam; // LookSAM every-k SAM-step gate (1=run 2nd bwd)
269	    // st.d_factor is NOT host-bound for the STAGED-d cell: the kernel's Prodigy
270	    // reduction stage computes it on-device (between B2 and P3) and stashes it.
271	    // st.param_init / st.prodigy_persist are device pointers bound by the cell.
272	}
273	
274	// Dispatch to the REAL per-element optimizer step. Each branch is a genuine,
275	// distinct call into csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h — there is no AdamW fallback.
276	template <OptId Opt>
277	__device__ __forceinline__ void apply_optimizer(
278	        float* __restrict__ params, const float* __restrict__ grad,
279	        int64_t idx, int step, const FusedOptState& st) {
280	    (void)step;  // referenced only by the cold-start branches (grokfast/grokadamw)
281	    if constexpr (Opt == OptId::AdamW) {
282	        algo::adamw_step<float, float>(
283	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, grad,
284	            st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd, st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
285	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::Lion) {
286	        algo::lion_step<float, float>(
287	            params, st.exp_avg, grad, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.wd, idx);
288	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::Grokfast) {
289	        // COLD-START (state-aware tail; owner baseline blocker (a)): the eager
290	        // Grokfast seeds the slow-grad EMA with the FIRST gradient, not zeros
291	        // (grokfast.py _group_cache: state["ema"] = grad0.clone()), because a
292	        // zero seed under-amplifies the early grokking phase and the kernel
293	        // applies no EMA bias correction. The persistent [m|v|extra] state cache
294	        // zero-inits ema=0, so at step 1 we must seed ema=grad HERE — then
295	        // grokfast_fused_step's e_new = alpha*g + (1-alpha)*g = g matches the
296	        // eager ema=grad0 exactly. Per-element on this thread's own idx (the P3
297	        // tail owns each element once), so no race / no barrier needed. For
298	        // step>1 the cache carries the real EMA forward (no reseed).
299	        if (step == 1) st.ema[idx] = grad[idx];
300	        algo::grokfast_fused_step<float, float>(
301	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, st.ema, grad,
302	            st.alpha, st.lamb, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
303	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
304	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::GrokAdamW) {
305	        // FAITHFUL GrokAdamW (decoder L3-TC conversion) — all THREE eager
306	        // mechanisms now land, so the cell is no longer a hollow pass:
307	        //
308	        //  (i)  PER-TENSOR LAYER-WISE β1 = β1·(1-γ)^layer (grokadamw.py
309	        //       _layer_beta1_by_id). The caller (the P3 work-steal loop, which
310	        //       owns the tensor index t == the flat named_parameters() layer
311	        //       index) has ALREADY rebased st.beta1 to β1_i AND st.bc1 to
312	        //       1-β1_i^step for THIS tensor before calling us (see the
313	        //       fused_decoder_megakernel P3 block, guarded by if constexpr
314	        //       GrokAdamW). So st.beta1/st.bc1 here are the per-tensor values;
315	        //       this branch just consumes them. bc2 stays global (β2 is not
316	        //       layer-wise). This is the mechanism that fails the STATE gate at
317	        //       step 1 if dropped (m-rel 0.895), so it is load-bearing.
318	        //
319	        //  (ii) GLOBAL GRAD-NORM CLIP to grad_clip (bindings.cpp
320	        //       clip_grad_norms_device_side → a GLOBAL norm over ALL tensors,
321	        //       one scalar clip_coef = grad_clip/(‖g‖₂+1e-6) applied to every
322	        //       grad when ‖g‖₂ > grad_clip). The kernel computes ‖g‖₂ + clip_coef
323	        //       ON-DEVICE in P2.5 (deterministic ascending-CTA reduction over the
324	        //       reduced grad) and stashes st.clip_coef; we scale the grad by it
325	        //       HERE. Eager clips IN-PLACE before the ema-seed AND the step, so we
326	        //       use the SAME clipped grad for both. At step 1 ‖g‖₂≈0.72<1 ⇒
327	        //       clip_coef=1 (inert), but it FIRES multi-step — the missing-clip
328	        //       2e-4 divergence is what the multi-step parity check catches.
329	        //
330	        //  (iii) ADAPTIVE α = alpha_init·exp(-κ·signal): in-context this is a
331	        //       genuine NO-OP. No race/gate path feeds (train_loss, val_loss) to
332	        //       GrokAdamW.step(), so eager α stays at alpha_init for ALL steps =
333	        //       the static st.alpha bound here. Faithful, not dropped (verified:
334	        //       fused_train_step/fused_optimizer_step/race never pass losses).
335	        //
336	        // COLD-START: eager seeds ema = the UNCLIPPED grad0, NOT the clipped grad.
337	        // grokadamw.py _group_cache clones state["ema"] = p.grad.clone() (the raw
338	        // gradient) BEFORE grokadamw_fused_step's in-place clip_grad_norms_device_
339	        // side (bindings.cpp:215) runs — so the cold-start seed is the UNCLIPPED
340	        // grad while the EMA filter input + amplification use the CLIPPED grad. The
341	        // prior `st.ema[idx]=gc` seeded the CLIPPED grad, which is byte-identical
342	        // when the clip is INERT (clip_coef==1 ⇒ gc==grad) — every currently-green
343	        // config — but diverges the m/ema state when the clip FIRES (the forced-fire
344	        // multi-step parity surfaced this: kernel ema/clipped==1.0 vs eager 1/coef).
345	        // Fix: seed the UNCLIPPED grad; keep the filter + g_amp on gc.
346	        const float gc = grad[idx] * st.clip_coef;   // (ii) global-clipped grad
347	        if (step == 1) st.ema[idx] = grad[idx];       // cold-start on UNCLIPPED grad
348	        // EMA filter + amplification (csrc/algorithms/grokadamw.h math), on gc.
349	        const float ema_new = st.alpha * st.ema[idx] + (1.0f - st.alpha) * gc;
350	        st.ema[idx] = ema_new;
351	        const float g_amp = gc + st.lamb * ema_new;
352	        // Adam moments + decoupled-WD apply: the canonical grokadamw_adam_tail
353	        // (bit-identical to grokadamw_step's tail), driven by the per-tensor
354	        // st.beta1/st.bc1 (i) and the un-inverted global st.bc2.
355	        float m_out, v_out, p_out;
356	        algo::grokadamw_adam_tail(
357	            g_amp, params[idx], st.exp_avg[idx], st.exp_avg_sq[idx],
358	            st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd, st.bc1, st.bc2,
359	            m_out, v_out, p_out);
360	        st.exp_avg[idx]    = m_out;
361	        st.exp_avg_sq[idx] = v_out;
362	        params[idx]        = p_out;
363	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::LookSAM) {
364	        algo::looksam_apply_step<float, float>(
365	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, st.sam_dir, grad,
366	            st.alpha, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
367	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
368	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::Prodigy) {
369	        algo::prodigy_apply_step<float, float>(
370	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, st.s_track, grad,
371	            st.d_factor, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
372	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
373	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::NeuralGrok) {
374	        // psi_b2 is the scalar packed immediately after psi_W2 in the `extra`
375	        // buffer (extra[kPsiB2Off] == st.psi_W2[kPsiHidden]). Read it ON-DEVICE
376	        // here, where the pointer is dereferenceable — the host cell cannot
377	        // deref a device pointer, so it leaves st.psi_b2 at its 0.0f default.
378	        // This threads the real psi_b2 bias (previously stuck at 0.0).
379	        const float psi_b2 = (st.psi_W2 != nullptr) ? st.psi_W2[kPsiHidden]
380	                                                     : st.psi_b2;
381	        const float psi = algo::neuralgrok_psi_forward<kPsiHidden>(
382	            fabsf(grad[idx]), st.psi_W1, st.psi_b1, st.psi_W2, psi_b2);
383	        algo::neuralgrok_apply_step<float, float>(
384	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, grad, psi,
385	            st.alpha, st.beta, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
386	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
387	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::Muon) {
388	        // 2D params: NS-orthogonalized direction precomputed; tail is the
389	        // momentum-decayed scaled apply. (1D params use AdamW upstream.)
390	        algo::muon_update_step<float>(
391	            params, st.orth, st.neg_lr_scale, st.decay_factor, idx);
392	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::SuperGrok11) {
393	        algo::sg11_sweep_b_step<float, float>(
394	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, grad, st.mu, st.gate,
395	            st.alpha, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
396	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
397	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::SuperGrok15) {
398	        algo::sg15_sweep_b_step<float, float>(
399	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, grad, st.mu, st.gate,
400	            st.alpha, st.alpha_max, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
401	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
402	    } else {  // OptId::SuperGrok2 — Adam apply on the meta-net smart gradient.
403	        // The CSA/HCA+PEER meta-net (separate launch) produced st.smart_grad;
404	        // the fused tail is the real Adam apply on it (faithful to the per-op
405	        // SG2 path's apply stage).
406	        const float* g = (st.smart_grad != nullptr) ? st.smart_grad : grad;
407	        algo::adamw_step<float, float>(
408	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, g,
409	            st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd, st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
410	    }
411	}

5	// stages for the 9 non-trivial optimizers (Phase 3 BUILD).

7	// WHY THIS HEADER EXISTS
8	// ----------------------
9	// opt_components.cuh::apply_optimizer<OptId> is the per-element TAIL. Today only
10	// AdamW / Lion have a complete in-kernel tail because they need no precompute.
11	// The other tails READ fields of FusedOptState (opt_components.cuh:84-113) that
12	// some upstream stage must PRODUCE per step:
13	//   * prodigy   reads st.d_factor       — a cross-ALL-tensors r/s reduction → d.
14	//   * muon      reads st.orth (+scales) — Newton-Schulz orthogonalization of a
15	//                                          2D tensor (5 matmul iterations).
16	//   * supergrok11 reads st.mu + st.gate — a per-element meta-MLP forward, then a
17	//                                          per-TENSOR cosine reduction.
18	//   * supergrok15 reads st.mu (+ st.gate is a host scalar) — meta-MLP forward.
19	// grokfast / grokadamw / neuralgrok need NOTHING (their precompute is already
20	// fused INTO their apply math — see the verdict block below). looksam needs a
21	// SAM-direction the MODEL produces on sam steps (it cannot be a pure optimizer
22	// stage). supergrok2 is owned by a sibling agent and is OUT OF SCOPE here.
23	//
24	// This header provides `optimizer_precompute_stage<OptId>(...)` device functions
25	// (one specialization per optimizer that needs one) that compute exactly those
26	// fields, by CALLING the canonical per-element math in csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h —
27	// never re-inlining it (scripts/check_math_single_source.py / the drift guard
28	// enforce that). Each transcription cites its semantic source by file:line.
29	//
30	// SCOPE / HONESTY (per csrc/fused/COMPONENT_CONTRACT.md):
31	//   * NO functionality suppressed; every stage is the REAL precompute.
32	//   * Self-contained: #includes the substrate + the canonical algorithm headers
33	//     + CUDA only (portability rule 1).
34	//   * No hidden state: all state flows through explicit pointers / the documented
35	//     PODs (rule 2).
36	//   * DETERMINISTIC reductions only — NO float atomicAdd. Cross-CTA partials use
37	//     an owner-computes tree (per-CTA slot in global memory → grid barrier → one
38	//     owner thread sums slots in FIXED index order). This is a deliberate,
39	//     contract-mandated DEVIATION from the live per-op kernels, which reduce with
40	//     atomicAdd (prodigy_sm90.cuh:105-108,135-138); math-equivalent in exact
41	//     arithmetic, fp32 summation order now fixed/reproducible. Within a single
42	//     CTA we use the existing deterministic warp+smem tree (primitives.cuh:125,
43	//     block_reduce_sum_f32 / :153 block_reduce_sum2_f32) — fixed thread count ⇒
44	//     fixed order.
45	//   * fp32 throughout (matches the per-op kernels and FusedOptState fields).
46	//   * NO builds / NO GPU runs in this phase: the CPU fp64 mirrors in
47	//     tests/hw/test_opt_stages.py ARE the validation of the staged algorithm;
48	//     the CUDA compile of this header is deferred (the megakernel codegen wiring
49	//     is specified in INTEGRATION-OPTSTAGES.md, owned at integration time).
50	//
51	// PER-OPTIMIZER VERDICT (full table — see the report + INTEGRATION-OPTSTAGES.md):
52	//   grokfast    NOTHING-NEEDED  EMA fused in apply (grokfast.h:63-65).

55	//                               229 → neuralgrok.h:31-46).

90	// =========================================================================
91	//  PrecomputeWorkspace — global scratch the cross-CTA stages reduce through.
92	//
93	//  Grouped as one POD (like PersistentContext) so the codegen kernel signature
94	//  stays uniform. The host allocates each pointer the chosen optimizer needs and
95	//  zero-fills the rest (a stage touches ONLY its optimizer's buffers). All FP32.
96	//
97	//  DETERMINISM: `partials` is a per-CTA slot array (length >= ctx.n_ctas, or
98	//  2*n_ctas for the two-value prodigy reduce). Each CTA writes its OWN slot (no
99	//  contention, no atomic); after a grid barrier, one owner thread sums the slots
100	//  in ascending index order — a fixed, reproducible fp32 summation. This is the
101	//  "owner-computes tree" that REPLACES the live path's atomicAdd accumulate.
102	// =========================================================================
103	struct PrecomputeWorkspace {
104	    // Prodigy: r/s partial slots (2 per CTA: [0..n_ctas) = r, [n_ctas..) = s)
105	    // and the reduced d output (a single device scalar the apply reads via
106	    // st.d_factor). d_prev is carried in by the cell.
107	    float* prodigy_partials = nullptr;   // length >= 2 * n_ctas
108	    float* prodigy_d        = nullptr;   // length 1 (reduced d; also st.d_factor)
109	    // Muon: Newton-Schulz scratch for ONE matrix at a time (rows*cols floats
110	    // each), plus a per-CTA Frobenius-norm partial slot array.
111	    float* muon_buf  = nullptr;          // momentum buffer (rows*cols), persists
112	    float* muon_X    = nullptr;          // current iterate           (rows*cols)
113	    float* muon_A    = nullptr;          // A = X Xᵀ  (rows*rows)
114	    float* muon_AX   = nullptr;          // A X       (rows*cols)
115	    float* muon_AAX  = nullptr;          // A (A X)   (rows*cols)
116	    float* muon_orth = nullptr;          // NS output = st.orth        (rows*cols)
117	    float* muon_nrm_partials = nullptr;  // length >= n_ctas (‖buf‖_F² partials)
118	    float* muon_inv_norm     = nullptr;  // length 1 (1/(‖buf‖_F + 1e-7))
119	};

121	// =========================================================================
122	//  Deterministic cross-CTA owner-computes sum.
123	//
124	//  Each CTA (its leader thread) has already published `my_partial` into
125	//  `slots[blockIdx.x]`. After the caller's grid barrier guarantees every slot is
126	//  visible, EVERY CTA's leader recomputes the SAME total by summing slots[0..
127	//  n-1] in ascending order. Fixed order ⇒ identical fp32 result on every CTA, no
128	//  atomics. Returns the total on the leader (thread 0); other threads return 0.
129	//  Caller broadcasts within the block if all threads need it.
130	// =========================================================================
131	__device__ __forceinline__ float owner_sum_slots(const float* __restrict__ slots,
132	                                                  unsigned n) {
133	    float acc = 0.0f;
134	    if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
135	        // Ascending fixed-index summation — deterministic fp32 order.
136	        for (unsigned i = 0; i < n; ++i) acc += slots[i];
137	    }
138	    return acc;
139	}

141	// ============================================================================
142	// (1) NOTHING-NEEDED — grokfast / grokadamw / neuralgrok.
143	//
144	// These have NO precompute stage on purpose; their would-be precompute is fused
145	// INTO the per-element apply (csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h), so apply_optimizer<>
146	// already runs a complete in-kernel tail. Documented here so the codegen's
147	// per-OptId dispatch can statically map them to "no stage" with a citation:
148	//
149	//   grokfast    grokfast.h:63-65  — `e_new = alpha*ema[idx] + (1-alpha)*g;
150	//                                     ema[idx]=e_new; g_amp = g + lamb*e_new;`
151	//                                     the slow-grad EMA UPDATE is inside
152	//                                     grokfast_fused_step, before its Adam tail.
153	//   grokadamw   grokadamw.h:48-49 — `ema_new = alpha*ema[idx] + (1-alpha)*g;
154	//                                     ema[idx]=ema_new;` inside grokadamw_step.
155	//   neuralgrok  opt_components.cuh:222-229 — apply_optimizer<NeuralGrok> calls
156	//                                     neuralgrok_psi_forward (neuralgrok.h:31-46)
157	//                                     per element, then neuralgrok_apply_step.
158	//                                     The psi MLP is a per-TENSOR weight set read
159	//                                     inline; there is no per-element precompute
160	//                                     buffer to fill.
161	//
162	// Compile-time assertion that no caller asks these for a stage.
163	// ============================================================================
164	template <OptId Opt>
165	struct optimizer_needs_precompute {
166	    static constexpr bool value =
167	        (Opt == OptId::Prodigy)     || (Opt == OptId::Muon) ||
168	        (Opt == OptId::SuperGrok11) || (Opt == OptId::SuperGrok15);
169	};

171	// ============================================================================
172	// (2) MODEL-COUPLED — looksam.
173	//
174	// looksam_apply_step (looksam.h:63-91) reads st.sam_dir, where on a SAM step
175	//   sam_dir[idx] = g_sam[idx] − g[idx]                       (looksam.h:52-59)
176	// and g_sam is the gradient at the PERTURBED parameters p + rho·g/‖g‖
177	// (looksam.h:27-38) — i.e. the output of a SECOND model backward. A pure
178	// optimizer stage CANNOT produce it: it requires re-running the model forward+
179	// backward at perturbed weights, which is the MODEL's job, not the optimizer's.
180	//
181	// CONTRACT (NOT faked here): the megakernel exposes `st.sam_dir` as an INPUT the
182	// MODEL STAGE fills on sam steps (every k steps), exactly as the per-op LookSAM
183	// path computes it from a separate SAM backward. On intervening (non-SAM) steps
184	// the cached sam_dir from the last SAM step is reused verbatim (looksam.h:1-19,
185	// "reused as a cached direction"). There is therefore NO looksam specialization
186	// of optimizer_precompute_stage — by design. See INTEGRATION-OPTSTAGES.md for
187	// the model-stage → sam_dir wiring.
188	// ============================================================================
189	
190	// ============================================================================
191	// (3a) STAGED — PRODIGY: cross-ALL-tensors d-adaptation reduction.
192	//
193	// Shape: GLOBAL. r and s are sums over EVERY element of EVERY parameter tensor
194	// (one scalar d for the whole model). Semantic source — the per-op three-kernel
195	// orchestration: prodigy_reduce_kernel (prodigy_sm90.cuh:85-109) accumulates the
196	// per-element partials via prodigy_partials_step, then prodigy_update_d
197	// (prodigy.h:56-65) combines them into d. The multi-tensor live driver is
198	// launch_multi_tensor_prodigy_fused_reduce_step (prodigy_sm90.cuh:465-544).
199	//
200	// IN-KERNEL vs HOST split (faithful to the live path):
201	//   * IN-KERNEL (this stage): the per-step Σ r_local / Σ s_local over all tensors
202	//     (prodigy_partials_step, prodigy.h:28-53) + prodigy_update_d (prodigy.h:56-
203	//     65). This is the cross-tensor reduction Audit-C flagged.
204	//   * HOST / CELL (NOT in this stage — documented, not hidden): the PERSISTENT
205	//     beta3-EMA decay of (r,s) across steps and the d_coef scaling live in the
206	//     host launcher (prodigy_sm90.cuh:488-521 / bindings.cpp:1246-1264), outside
207	//     prodigy.h. The grokking race uses that EMA estimator. The in-kernel stage
208	//     here computes the INSTANTANEOUS Σ-partials + max() update (d0=1e-6 init);
209	//     a cell wanting the EMA form decays prodigy_partials in the workspace
210	//     before the barrier and scales before prodigy_update_d — see
211	//     INTEGRATION-OPTSTAGES.md. The DEVICE math (prodigy.h) is byte-unchanged.
212	//
213	// DETERMINISM: REPLACES prodigy_sm90.cuh's atomicAdd (:105-108,:135-138) with
214	//   per-CTA (r,s) slot publish → grid barrier → owner-computes fixed-order sum →
215	//   prodigy_update_d. No float atomic.
216	//
217	// TWO-PHASE STAGE (the caller drives the barrier between them so the codegen owns
218	// the grid sync, consistent with fused_megakernel.cuh's phase pipeline):
219	//   Phase A: each CTA drains the task queue, accumulates this CTA's (r,s) over
220	//            its claimed tensors, publishes to ws.prodigy_partials slots.
221	//   [caller grid barrier — every slot visible]
222	//   Phase B: every CTA owner-sums the slots in fixed order and writes d to
223	//            ws.prodigy_d (== st.d_factor for the apply tail).
224	// ============================================================================
225	
226	// Phase A — accumulate this CTA's (r,s) partial over all its queued tensors and
227	// publish to the per-CTA slots. `param_init` is the Prodigy trajectory anchor
228	// (one flat blob parallel to params). Drains the SAME task queue the apply uses.
229	__device__ inline void prodigy_precompute_reduce_phaseA(
230	        const PersistentContext& ctx,
231	        const float* __restrict__ params,
232	        const float* __restrict__ param_init,
233	        const float* __restrict__ grad,
234	        const int* __restrict__ sizes, const int* __restrict__ offsets,
235	        float d_prev,
236	        PrecomputeWorkspace ws) {
237	    __shared__ int task_slot;
238	    float r_acc = 0.0f, s_acc = 0.0f;
239	    TaskQueue q = ctx.queue();
240	    for (int t = q.next_block(&task_slot); t < ctx.n_tasks;
241	         t = q.next_block(&task_slot)) {
242	        const int n = sizes[t];
243	        const int64_t off = (int64_t)offsets[t];
244	        for (int i = threadIdx.x; i < n; i += blockDim.x) {
245	            // Canonical per-element partials (prodigy.h:28-53). r/s carry d² so
246	            // d_hat=r/s is scale-free; s is the L1 norm Σ d²·|g|.
247	            float r_one = 0.0f, s_one = 0.0f;
248	            algo::prodigy_partials_step(params + off, param_init + off, grad + off,
249	                                        d_prev, (int64_t)i, r_one, s_one);
250	            r_acc += r_one;
251	            s_acc += s_one;
252	        }
253	    }
254	    // Deterministic in-CTA reduction of this CTA's (r,s) — fixed thread count.
255	    float r_block, s_block;
256	    prim::block_reduce_sum2_f32(r_acc, s_acc, r_block, s_block);
257	    if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
258	        // Per-CTA slot publish (no atomic). r slots [0..n_ctas), s slots after.
259	        ws.prodigy_partials[blockIdx.x]              = r_block;
260	        ws.prodigy_partials[ctx.n_ctas + blockIdx.x] = s_block;
261	    }
262	}
263	
264	// Phase B — owner-computes deterministic sum of all CTA slots, then the canonical
265	// d update. Runs AFTER the caller's grid barrier. Every CTA writes the same d
266	// (redundant but race-free); the apply reads ws.prodigy_d via st.d_factor.
267	__device__ inline void prodigy_precompute_reduce_phaseB(
268	        const PersistentContext& ctx, float d_prev, PrecomputeWorkspace ws) {
269	    if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
270	        // Fixed-order sums (ascending CTA index) — deterministic fp32.
271	        float r_sum = 0.0f, s_sum = 0.0f;
272	        for (unsigned c = 0; c < ctx.n_ctas; ++c) {
273	            r_sum += ws.prodigy_partials[c];
274	            s_sum += ws.prodigy_partials[ctx.n_ctas + c];
275	        }
276	        // Canonical d update (prodigy.h:56-65): d = max(d_prev, r/|s|).
277	        ws.prodigy_d[0] = algo::prodigy_update_d(d_prev, r_sum, s_sum);
278	    }
279	}
